title: When Most Life Vanished
question: What turns ordinary extinction into a mass extinction, and what follows one?
hook: Species disappear all the time, yet in the Great Dying about 81% of marine species were lost.
idea: A mass extinction is a rapid, widespread loss of life in which species die out faster than the background rate and faster than new ones arise.

beats.prompt: Put the steps of a leading explanation for the Kellwasser extinction in order.
items: Rivers carry land nutrients into the ocean
Dying algae decompose and use up dissolved oxygen
beats.explain: Nutrients feed huge algal blooms; when the algae die and rot they consume the water's oxygen, and the resulting anoxic conditions kill sea life.

beats.prompt: Sort each group of living things by the extinction that hit it.
beats.explain: The Late Devonian events took out placoderms and tropical seabed animals such as jawless fish, while the Great Dying ended dominant coral groups and cut short many synapsid lineages.

beats.prompt: The Great Dying cut short many lineages of synapsids, the mammal relatives living on land. With their places left empty, what happens next?

choices.label: The surviving mammal relatives quickly refill every niche
choices.feedback: Tempting, since survivors usually bounce back, but vertebrate recovery took 30 million years and another group seized the openings.

choices.label: Archosaurs, dinosaur and crocodile relatives, diversify into the empty niches
Land stays almost empty of vertebrates for good
choices.feedback: Recovery was slow, but it did happen; the empty niches were eventually filled.

choices.label: Trilobites crawl ashore and take over
choices.feedback: Trilobites were sea creatures, and they themselves went extinct in the Great Dying.

beats.explain: Vertebrates took 30 million years to recover, and the vacant niches gave archosaurs the opportunity to diversify.

beats.prompt: Match each extinction to what it is known for.
pairs: End of the armored placoderm fish
beats.explain: Each event left a different mark: microbes in the Great Oxidation Event, reefs in the Kellwasser, placoderms in the Hangenberg, and the biggest toll of all in the Great Dying.
